mainTopic: Why רב had to rule separately that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, and what that tells us about a dispute that appears only in a ברייתא (the case of a nursing animal bought from a גוי).
overview: רב ruled that the הלכה follows this whole chapter, and also that it follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם. The גמרא explains that the second ruling shows 'the whole chapter' refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and that a disagreement found only in a ברייתא is not a real dispute. It then quotes that ברייתא: the תנא קמא says an animal bought from a גוי may be nursing a calf out of mercy, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל presumes she is its mother. The גמרא asks whether his presumption means only that she has given birth, or also that the calf she nurses is hers. That would matter for lashes under אותו ואת בנו. Several proofs are brought and all are rejected. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that a pig-like animal following a ewe exempts her from בכורה but is forbidden to eat 'until אליהו comes'. After rejecting the idea that he was unsure of the הלכה, the גמרא explains that he follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל but was unsure whether, in that view, a mother that gave birth might nurse young that are not hers, even of another species. The amud ends as the גמרא begins showing that רבי יוחנן's statement was a dilemma, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why is the specific ruling needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם' if he already ruled that the הלכה follows the whole chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם — why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one of רב's rulings as seemingly unnecessary. רב already said the הלכה follows the whole chapter, so the extra ruling looks repeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a teacher like רב does not say anything extra for no reason. If 'the whole chapter' already includes רבי יוסי בן המשולם, saying his name separately seems redundant. The גמרא wants to find what new information the extra ruling adds.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the general ruling that the הלכה follows the whole chapter should already include him.

steps.title: What we would have mistakenly thought
steps.stepSummary: Without the specific ruling, we might have thought that 'the whole chapter' meant only רבי יוסי בן המשולם's two rulings. We would also have thought that a ברייתא-only disagreement counts as a real dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose רב had said only 'the הלכה follows the whole chapter' and had not said 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.' Then I would have said he meant רבי יוסי בן המשולם. And why would he say 'the whole chapter'? Because רבי יוסי said two things in it. I would also have thought that a disagreement found in a ברייתא counts as a real dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer with a הוה אמינא, a mistaken first impression we would have had without the extra ruling. This sets up the real conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'the whole chapter' sounds like more than one case. Someone could explain it as covering רבי יוסי בן המשולם's two separate statements. That reading would leave out the משנה that is challenged only by a ברייתא, because a ברייתא disagreement would count as a true dispute.

steps.title: What the specific ruling actually teaches
steps.stepSummary: Because רב named רבי יוסי separately, 'the whole chapter' must refer to the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A ברייתא-only disagreement is not a real dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught us 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי' in order to teach us that 'the whole chapter' refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and that a disagreement in a ברייתא is not a real dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. The separate ruling for רבי יוסי frees 'the whole chapter' to mean something else: the משנה that matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי בן המשולם got his own ruling, 'the whole chapter' cannot be about him alone. It must also cover the משנה that agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. That משנה stays authoritative because a disagreement found only in a ברייתא does not count as a true dispute against it.

steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading of רב, a משנה that is opposed only in a ברייתא is not considered disputed. Its view (here, matching רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) stands as the הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for how much weight to give a ברייתא that disagrees with a משנה. A ברייתא-only disagreement does not cancel the authority of the משנה.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a nursing animal bought from a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes a תנא קמא who says the next calf is a ספק בכור, because an animal may nurse a calf that is not hers. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we keep the presumption (חזקה) that she is the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Someone buys a nursing animal from a גוי. The next calf she gives birth to is a בכור because of the doubt, since an animal may nurse another animal's young out of mercy even if she has never given birth. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the matter stays in its presumed state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. The first, unnamed opinion treats the next calf as a possible בכור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל assumes the nursing animal is the mother of the calf she is nursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal has already given birth (to the calf she nurses), her next calf is not a בכור. The תנא קמא doubts that she is the mother, since animals sometimes nurse others' young out of mercy, so the next calf may be a בכור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל relies on the חזקה that she is the mother, which matches the משנה in our chapter.

steps.title: The flock that gave birth at night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a second ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A farmer finds male calves nursing from animals that gave birth before, and female calves nursing from first-time mothers. He does not worry that the calves switched mothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל used to say: Someone goes into his flock at night. He sees about ten or fifteen animals giving birth, some for the first time and some not. The next morning he finds the males nursing from the animals that gave birth before, and the females nursing from the first-time mothers. He does not need to worry that one mother's calf wandered over to another mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא from step 5. It adds a second example of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule that a nursing animal is presumed to be the calf's mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The males are nursing from mothers whose calves are not a בכור anyway. The females are nursing from first-time mothers, and a female is never a בכור. If we trust that each calf is with its real mother, then there is no בכור here at all. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we may trust that, and we need not suspect a male actually came from a first-time mother.

steps.title: What exactly does the presumption mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's חזקה. Does it mean only that a nursing animal has given birth, so she might still nurse another's calf? Or does it mean she nurses only her own calf?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: When רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said 'the matter stays in its חזקה,' what did he mean? Maybe he meant that an animal does not show mercy and nurse unless she has given birth. If so, once she has given birth, we do worry that she might nurse another's calf. Or maybe he meant that she nurses only her own calf and not a calf that is not hers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question (איבעיא) about the exact scope of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's presumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings agree that a nursing animal has surely given birth, so her next calf is not a בכור. They differ on whether the calf she is nursing is surely her own. Under the first reading, she might be nursing another animal's calf out of mercy.

steps.title: The difference: lashes for slaughtering mother and young
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether someone gets lashes for slaughtering the animal and the calf it nurses on the same day, under אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is about getting lashes for violating אותו ואת בנו. If she nurses only her own calf, the calf is definitely hers, so he gets lashes. If she might also nurse a calf that is not hers, it is only a doubt, so he does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 8. The two readings differ on lashes for slaughtering a mother and her young on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes require certainty that the איסור was broken. If an animal nurses only her own calf, the nursing calf is certainly her child, and he gets lashes. If she may nurse others' calves too, the relationship is only a ספק, and no lashes are given.

steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from a משנה that the animal nurses only her own calf. There, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that someone who buys a nursing animal from a גוי need not worry that the calf belongs to another animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the answer? Come and hear: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Someone who buys an animal from a גוי does not need to worry that perhaps it was the calf of another animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to settle the dilemma of step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we do not suspect that the nursing calf belongs to a different animal. That sounds like the second reading: an animal nurses only her own calf. If so, the answer would be that he gets lashes.

steps.title: The proof fails: 'was', not 'is'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה says 'was', not 'is'. It means only that she must have had a calf of her own before, since she would not nurse otherwise. It does not say that the calf she is nursing now is hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the משנה say 'it IS another's calf'? It says 'it WAS'! This is what it means: Don't worry that she is nursing another's calf and never gave birth herself. She would not nurse unless she already had a calf of her own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof of step 10 by reading the exact wording of the משנה carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'היה' (was) shows that the משנה is only telling us the animal has already given birth, so her next calf is not a בכור. That fits the first reading as well. She may still be nursing another animal's calf out of mercy. So the dilemma of step 7 is left unresolved by this source.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the mothers that already gave birth before are nursing, and still we do not worry that they are nursing someone else's calf. So it seems we assume each mother nurses only her own baby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Step 11, the גמרא tries a new proof from the continuation of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a nursing animal nurses only her own calf
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of the משנה about a farmer who sees his flock nursing

steps.title: Why the flock case seems to prove the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. Why don't we worry that a mother is showing mercy to someone else's calf? It must be that she nurses only her own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? Let us worry that perhaps a mother is showing mercy and nursing a calf that is not hers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the logic of the proof by asking why we are not worried. Since the משנה says not to worry, it seems a mother never nurses another's calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If mothers sometimes nursed other calves out of mercy, the farmer should have to worry about the experienced mothers. The משנה's 'no worry' seems to show that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds a mother nurses only her own calf.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let us be concerned
She surely shows mercy (nursing a calf out of compassion)

phrases.english: Why not?
Let us worry that perhaps she is showing mercy (to another's calf)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the source in Step 12 counts as a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a nursing animal nurses only her own calf
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the משנה does not worry about mercy-nursing

steps.title: A mother will not leave her own calf for another
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. In the flock case each mother's own calf is right there, and a mother will not abandon her own calf to nurse a stranger's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where her own calf is present, she does not leave her own and show mercy to one that is not hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if mothers do sometimes nurse another's calf out of mercy, a mother would not do so while her own calf is right there. In the flock all the calves are present, so each mother nurses her own. This tells us nothing about a mother whose own calf may be missing, like the one bought from a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where her own (calf) is
She leaves / abandons
She shows mercy

phrases.english: In a place where her own (calf) is,
she does not leave her own
and show mercy to one that is not hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Steps 12–13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The flock case only, which has all calves present
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignores that in the flock each mother's own calf is present. That situation is different from a lone nursing animal.

steps.title: A proof from the word 'and similarly' in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement 'דבר בחזקתו'. The first clause (bought from a גוי) seems to be compared to the second clause (the flock) with the word 'וכן'. Since the calves in the second clause are certainly the mothers' own, the calf in the first clause should be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'The matter stays in its presumed status, etc.' Isn't the first clause like the last clause? Just as in the last clause the calf is certainly hers, so too in the first clause the calf is certainly hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another proof, this time from how the two halves of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling are linked by 'וכן' ('and similarly').
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכן' suggests the two cases share the same law. In the flock case the calves are certainly the mothers' own, so the calf of an animal bought from a גוי would also be certainly hers.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter stays in its presumed status
The first clause
The last clause
Similar to
Certainly

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'The matter stays in its presumed status, etc.'
Is it not that the first clause is similar to the last clause?
Just as in the last clause (the calf) is certainly hers,
so too in the first clause it is certainly hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the flock proof was rejected, the גמרא tries to prove the point by linking the two clauses together.
steps.raayaObject: That a nursing animal nurses only her own calf
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'וכן' connecting the two clauses of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling

steps.title: The two clauses are different cases
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The two clauses are not truly comparable. Each stays as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these really comparable? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison between the two clauses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the flock case all the calves are present, so each mother certainly nurses her own. In the case of the animal bought from a גוי, her own calf may not be there, so the calf is not certainly hers. The same word 'וכן' does not make the cases identical.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? (a phrase rejecting a comparison)
As it is (each case stands on its own)

phrases.english: Are these comparable?
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? הַאי כִּדְאִיתֵאּ, וְהַאי כִּדְאִיתֵאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the first and last clause
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes 'וכן' makes the cases identical. In fact they describe different situations: the calves present versus a calf that may not be hers.

steps.title: Then what does 'and similarly' mean?
steps.stepSummary: If the clauses are different, the גמרא asks what the word 'וכן' is comparing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'and similarly' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the shared point of the two clauses is, since 'וכן' must mean something. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having separated the two cases, the גמרא must explain why the ברייתא links them at all. It asks what they have in common.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of 'and similarly'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rejection in Step 16: if the cases differ, what does 'וכן' mean?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the two clauses share, as shown by the word 'וכן'

steps.title: Both clauses agree only about the exemption from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: 'וכן' refers only to the exemption from בכורה. In both cases the mother has clearly given birth before, so her next calf is not a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to the exemption from the firstborn law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two clauses share only one point: in both, the mother is exempt from בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the nursing proves the mother has given birth before, so her future calves are not a בכור. Whether the calf she is nursing now is hers is a different question, and 'וכן' does not address it.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt
The law of the firstborn animal

steps.whatToRemember: All the proofs are rejected. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule only proves that a nursing animal has given birth before, which exempts her next calf from בכורה. It does not prove that the calf she is nursing is her own.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two questions. 'Has she given birth?' is settled by the nursing, and it matters for בכורה. 'Is this calf hers?' is still open, and it matters for אותו ואת בנו.

phrases.english: It refers to the exemption from the firstborn law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וכן' links the clauses only regarding the exemption from בכורה, not regarding whether the calf is the mother's own.

steps.title: A pig-like animal following a ewe
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן. If a pig-like animal is seen trailing after a ewe, the ewe is exempt from בכורה. The animal is forbidden to eat until אליהו comes and decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone saw a pig-like animal attached to a ewe and following her, the ewe is exempt from בכורה, and the animal is forbidden to eat 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רבי יוחנן. It connects to the earlier discussion about whether a nursing animal is presumed to be the mother's own baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ewe is treated as if she gave birth to this creature, so her womb is already 'opened' and her next baby is not a בכור. Yet the creature itself is forbidden to eat, as if it might really be a pig and not her baby. The verse 'until he comes' hints that only אליהו can settle the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Pig (here, an animal that looks like a pig)
Attached to and following after (like a nursing baby)
Ewe (female sheep)
Exempt from the firstborn law (her next baby is not a בכור)
'Until he comes and teaches righteousness to you' (הושע 10:12), meaning until אליהו decides

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up who is exempt and who is forbidden. The EWE is exempt from בכורה. The PIG-LIKE ANIMAL is the one forbidden to eat.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If one saw a pig-like animal trailing after a ewe,
phrases.notes: It looks like it is her nursing baby.

phrases.english: she (the ewe) is exempt from the firstborn law,
phrases.notes: Her next baby will not be a בכור.

phrases.english: and it (the pig-like animal) is forbidden to eat
'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you.'
phrases.notes: Until אליהו comes and decides.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the meaning of 'וכן' in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement, the גמרא brings a related case about whether a following or nursing animal is presumed to be the mother's own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ewe is exempt from בכורה. The pig-like animal is forbidden to eat until אליהו decides.

steps.title: The two halves follow opposite opinions
steps.stepSummary: The exemption from בכורה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who presumes the follower is her baby. The ban on eating follows the רבנן, who do not presume this. That is inconsistent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Exempt from בכורה: whose view is that? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's. Forbidden to eat: that is the רבנן's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling. His two halves seem to follow two opposing opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that an animal following the mother is presumed to be hers. That explains why the ewe is exempt from בכורה. The רבנן hold that a mother might nurse a stranger, which explains why the creature might be a real pig and is forbidden. You cannot logically hold both views at once.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (whose opinion is this?)
The Sages (the majority opinion)

phrases.english: Exempt from the firstborn law: according to whom?
According to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
phrases.notes: He presumes the following animal is her baby.

phrases.english: and forbidden to eat: according to the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: They do not presume it is her baby, so it may be a real pig.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling just quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's two-part ruling about the pig-like animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exemption assumes the animal is the ewe's baby, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds. The eating ban assumes it might not be hers, as the רבנן hold. One ruling cannot follow two opposite opinions.

steps.title: The verse 'until he comes' does not fit
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבי יוחנן follows the רבנן, the doubt is a factual question about who the mother is. He should have said 'until the matter becomes known,' not 'until אליהו comes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, if he follows the רבנן, why say 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you'? He should have said 'until the matter becomes known to you'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge about the wording of רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the problem is factual: we do not know if this creature is really the ewe's baby. Such a doubt could be cleared up by finding out the facts. The phrase 'until אליהו comes' sounds like a doubt about the הלכה itself, which only a prophet can settle.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another challenge)
Until the matter becomes known to you (used for a factual doubt)
He should have said

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it follows the Rabbis,
what is 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you'?
phrases.notes: This phrase suggests a doubt about the הלכה.

phrases.english: He should have said 'until the matter becomes known to you'!
phrases.notes: This phrase would fit a doubt about the facts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate attack on the same ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of the verse 'עד יבא ויורה צדק לכם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the רבנן the doubt is factual (who is the mother?). A factual doubt calls for 'until it becomes known,' not for waiting for אליהו to settle the הלכה.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי יוחנן was unsure of the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests an answer. Maybe רבי יוחנן was unsure whether the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or the רבנן. That would explain mixing both views and citing 'until אליהו comes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: he was uncertain whether the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or the רבנן,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to both challenges. It is setting it up only so that it can knock it down in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן did not know which opinion is the הלכה, he would be strict both ways, and that explains the mixed ruling. It would also explain the verse, because this is now a doubt about the הלכה, which fits 'until אליהו comes.'

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer, often to be rejected)
He is in doubt about it

phrases.english: And if you will say: he was uncertain

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: whether the halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
or the Rabbis,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the challenges in steps 20 and 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proposed answer: the ruling reflects a doubt about which opinion is the הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to mix two opposing opinions, and the verse seemed out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: If רבי יוחנן was unsure of the הלכה, being strict both ways and waiting for אליהו would make sense. This answer is rejected in the next steps.

steps.title: Doubt does not explain a full exemption
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן was in doubt, he should not have given the ewe a clear exemption from בכורה. A doubt would only make her next baby a doubtful בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was uncertain, why is she exempt from בכורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer from step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being in doubt explains the strictness about eating. But it does not explain a clean exemption from בכורה. Under doubt, the ewe's next baby should be a possible בכור, not plainly exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?

phrases.english: If he was uncertain,
why is she exempt from the firstborn law?
phrases.notes: Doubt should lead to a doubtful status, not a full exemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ — אַמַּאי פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed answer of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'he was in doubt' answer as an explanation for the exemption half of the ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A doubt explains being strict, but not giving a full, clear exemption from בכורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן already ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: There is no room for doubt at all. רבי יוחנן himself ruled that the halacha follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wherever he appears in the משנה, except in three places. This case is not one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, was he really in doubt? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught in our משנה, the הלכה follows him, except for the guarantor, צידן, and the last case about evidence!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, stronger rejection of the 'he was unsure' answer. It quotes רבי יוחנן's own general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a fixed rule: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, with only three exceptions. Our case is not one of those three. So רבי יוחנן could not have been unsure here, and he should have ruled fully like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which would also permit eating. The original question returns in full force.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? (introduces a contradicting source)
The הלכה follows him
Guarantor (one exception, from בבא בתרא)
צידן, the city of a case in גיטין (another exception)
The final case about bringing evidence (סנהדרין, the third exception)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling about the pig-like animal seems to mix רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (exempt from בכורה) with the רבנן (forbidden to eat). Saying 'he was unsure' fails twice. A doubt cannot give a full exemption, and רבי יוחנן himself rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא uses a sage's own general rules to test his specific rulings. A specific ruling must match the general rule unless it falls under a listed exception.

phrases.english: And furthermore: was he really in doubt?
But didn't Rabba bar bar Ḥana say
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Wherever Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught
in our Mishna, the halacha follows him,
except for the guarantor, and Tzaidan,
phrases.notes: See בבא בתרא 174a and גיטין 74a.

phrases.english: and the final case about evidence!
phrases.notes: See סנהדרין 31a.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: מִי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rejection of the proposed answer in step 22, adding to the rejection in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the very idea that רבי יוחנן could be unsure which opinion is the הלכה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן's own general rule says the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, and this case is not among the three exceptions.

steps.title: The doubt is about what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was certain the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He was unsure whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a mother animal shows mercy to young that are not hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it was obvious to him that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But he was unsure whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that an animal that gave birth is merciful to young that are not hers, or is not merciful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to explain the 'until אליהו comes' ruling. The doubt is not about whom to follow. It is about what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל himself meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ewe gave birth, so her next baby is clearly not a בכור, and she is exempt from בכורה. The open question is whether this particular creature is her baby. If a mother that gave birth might nurse another's young out of mercy, it may not be hers. That question about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view can never be settled, so the ruling says 'until אליהו comes.'

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Signals a fresh answer that keeps the original assumption.
It is obvious to him
He is in doubt
An animal that has given birth
Shows mercy, meaning she nurses and cares for a baby

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 22. There the doubt was which תנא the הלכה follows. Here רבי יוחנן is sure the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He is only unsure how far that view goes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer settles both earlier problems. The exemption from בכורה is certain. The ban on eating comes from a doubt about a תנא's view, and only אליהו could clear that up.

phrases.english: Actually, it is obvious to him
that the halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
but he is uncertain

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָבַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: whether Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds
that an animal that has given birth is merciful (to young not her own),
phrases.notes: She might nurse another animal's baby because she has milk and feels motherly.

phrases.english: or is not merciful.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 22, as Step 24 required. The הלכה clearly follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and the doubt moves to the content of his view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the doubt from 'which opinion is הלכה' to 'what exactly the accepted opinion holds'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was unsure whether to follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or the רבנן (rejected in Steps 23–24).
steps.terutzMaskana: He follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל but is unsure whether a mother that gave birth might nurse young that are not hers. That doubt can only be settled by אליהו.

steps.title: Why not use a lamb and ask about lashes?
steps.stepSummary: If the doubt is about a mother's mercy, the case should use an ordinary lamb. The question would then be lashes under אותו ואת בנו for slaughtering a mother and its offspring on one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of teaching us the case of a pig, let him teach us the case of a lamb. Then he could ask whether one gets lashes for it because of 'it and its offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If the question is only about a mother's mercy, why pick the strange pig-like case and not a simple lamb?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same doubt would come up with a lamb following a ewe. Then the practical question would be whether slaughtering both on one day breaks אותו ואת בנו and earns lashes. The choice of a pig-like creature seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It opens a challenge built on the last answer.
Pig, here a pig-like creature following the ewe
Lamb
To receive lashes
The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and her young on the same day

phrases.english: If so,
instead of teaching us (the case of) a pig,
let him teach us (the case of) a lamb,
and (ask about) receiving lashes for it
because of (slaughtering) "it and its offspring"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, עַד דְּאַשְׁמְעִינַן חֲזִיר, לַישְׁמְעִינַן טָלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 25 by asking why the case was set up the way it was.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of a pig-like creature in רבי יוחנן's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubt of Step 25 applies just as well to a lamb. A simpler and more common case would have done the job, so the pig detail seems pointless.

steps.title: The pig case teaches mercy even across species
steps.stepSummary: A lamb case would suggest a mother's mercy is only for her own species. The pig case shows that even a creature of another species might be nursed out of mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pig case was needed. Had he taught a lamb, I would have said: even if רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a mother that gave birth is merciful, that is only to her own species, not to another species. So he teaches a pig: she may be merciful even to one not of her species, since we can say perhaps she showed mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the pig case was chosen. It teaches a bigger doubt that a lamb case would not show.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a lamb, we could think the doubt is only for babies of the same species. The pig-like case shows the doubt goes further: the ewe might even nurse a creature of another kind. So the creature cannot be eaten, since it might not be the ewe's baby.

steps.whatToRemember: The doubt in רבי יוחנן's ruling is whether, in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, a mother that gave birth might nurse another's young, even one of a different species. That is why the pig case is used.

phrases.english: The pig (case) was necessary for him,
for if he had taught us a lamb,
I would have said:
even if you say
that he holds a mother that gave birth is merciful,
that is to her own species,
but to one not of her species, no.
So he teaches us a pig, that she is merciful,
even to one not of her species too,
for one can say that perhaps she was merciful.

steps.title: Bringing in a supporting statement of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this explanation is what רבי יוחנן's statement really meant: it was a dilemma (בעי) that he raised and did not settle. The wording of the dilemma continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי יוחנן said: a dilemma was raised...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It shows that רבי יוחנן's statement was really phrased as a dilemma (בעי), which fits the explanation in steps 25–27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase והיינו ('and this is') ties the explanation to what רבי יוחנן said. The word בעי shows that his statement was an unsolved question he raised, which fits the idea that he was unsure about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view and so said 'until אליהו comes.' The wording of the dilemma appears on the next amud.
